items.note: S1.3.1 states the exchange (X,Y)->(-Y,X) over triples with every scratch wire restored, and quotes y_S -> y_S+x_S (line 730). It gives no h=100, neighbour rule or cancellation mechanism, and calls all three stages 'forward invocations' although stage 2 is the inverse schedule from Y to X (731-733).
S1.3.2 states the common frame per gate, the implemented operator D_out S D_in^{-1}, and the edge operator D_v D_u^{-1}, matching 812-817. It is an infer step, so nothing is derived.

S1.3.3 only says that nested nondegenerate subspaces of an m-dimensional space are attached and that s<Wm results. It omits F^{tensor 3}, that the only decreasing edges are central wires losing h, L=Ich, the budget Wm-2N+2L and L/N<1/2.
S1.3.4 gives the endpoint difference I_m, the shear H<-H+D on every role, and s_b<W_b m. It omits the projection assignment (P_U, -P_{U_a}) and the exact rank sum W_b m-N+2L_b.

S1.3.5 gives the phase frames C_U, edge differences as products of aI+bX_v, C^{tensor m} on every role, and s_c<W_c m. It omits 'or its inverse', the one-kernel-per-orthonormal-residual-vector count, the diagonal corrections and the exact s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c.
The plan states s_b<W_b m and s_c<W_c m, and uses s/W<m^tau in S2.3. It never gives the reason (L<N/2), the deficits eta, or the explicit tau=sigma=1-2^{-50} with its justification log m<20.
S1.1 and S1.2 faithfully list the elementary O(V) stream operations and the controlled shift and rational-unit scaling (with the b^{O(1)} offset condition in the quote).
S2.1 states E_1 Pi E_2 with lower-triangular invertible factors and a ones in Pi. S2.2 states exactly a interchanges plus O(V). Both are infer steps with no derivation.

S2.3 states e=m^k, the W row-split role streams, edges done by smaller interchanges, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) and O(Ve^tau). It omits the row-field divisibility by W^k and the three-step conversion of the shear into an interchange (1535-1541).
S2.4 states O(Vu^tau) for two disjoint u-bit fields of an arbitrary array, obtained by padding and taking high digits as rows. This is faithful in substance.

S3.1 follows the paper: H_0=bSCS, H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D, and s_c child calls on f=e/m axes plus binary basis changes. The conjugation by P_M that moves residual directions into coordinate slots is reduced to 'binary changes of basis', and the inverse-child identity (C^{-1})^{tensor f}=(-i)^f Z C Z is missing.

S3.2 gives the eight packed cyclic shifts, the restored third chunk, deterministic repair of an exponentially small exceptional set, and O(V(L^tau+1)). The delta_bad formula is not given but the content is right.

S3.3 alludes to a recursion on role streams of volume V/W with ratio below m. It gives no F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), no leaves at e<d^beta, no base-m pieces and no lambda' condition, and miscounts 's/W calls'.

S3 and its sub-steps follow the paper's route (C kernels, packed basis changes, network recursion on role streams, guard bits, single truncation) and state O(Vd^{lambda'}) with error below sqrt2 2^{-p}. The recurrence unrolling and the guard width Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) are only asserted, and the statement says d chunks where the paper has D<=d.

S4.1 gives the retained layout consumed by the opposite transform and the cost O(Tp[dK+pK^{tau-1}+l d^{lambda'}]). It omits F^+F^-=t^{-1}I, the bit-reversed order, the counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}, and the error bound.
S4.2 gives evaluation at a large power of two, the established O(N log N) multiplier, centered residues and O(rp log(rp)), matching the lemma.

S4.3 states f*g/(rM) with error below sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p}. S4's method and motivation give the paper's reason, that the pointwise product commutes with the retained order (P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v)). The normalization by M and the error accounting are not shown.

S5.1 gives P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA and S5.2 gives the tensor form RF_s=2^gamma B_0 QF_t A. Missing are the hypothesis theta=t/s-1>p/alpha^4, the definitions of P_s and P_t, and the fact that only approximations (error <p^2) are computed in that time.
S5.3 gives QF_t u = conj(a).(a*(conj(a).u))/T and says R cancels, but omits the chirp formula and the cancellation identity with its S^2 normalization.

S6.1 gives b, p=6b, d, K, T, axes of length r/2 or r, and distinct primes below t_i (S0 gives kappa). The other fixed rationals are missing, as are eta=1/(4d), alpha and gamma, and the prime window (1-2eta)t_i<s_i<=(1-eta)t_i is loosened to 'just below'.
Phi is named (S6.5 'applies Phi'; S6 'distinct prime axes') without its definition, the isomorphism or the triangular digit formula.
S6.3 describes twisting the last coordinate into the ring and untwisting, but gives no map x_d -> zeta y with zeta=e^{pi i/r}. Conservatively this counts as mentioned.

S6.4 composes A, chirp via complex convolution, B_0 and 2^gamma into RF_s, with the opposite sign by conjugation. S6.5 lists the six steps with scales S and 2^{2b+4}S, matching 4506-4534. The input scaling 2^{-b-2} is omitted, which is not essential.
S6.6 states error below 1/2, exact rounding and carries. It omits the error chain (E_s, E_w, 448b 2^{-3b/4}) and the role of gamma<=b/4 and p=6b.

S7 states that dividing by Tp=Theta(n) leaves seven powers at most 1-2kappa and absorbs polylog factors, matching 4983-4987. It does not list the seven terms or the minimal margin g_2=epsilon c(1-tau).
No step discusses the n log n conjecture or its negation.

errors.says: Three stages of forward invocations realize the exchange (X,Y)->(-Y,X).
errors.paper: Stages 1 and 3 are forward invocations from X to Y; stage 2 is the inverse forward schedule from Y to X, which effects X<-X-Y.

errors.says: s/W calls on role streams of volume V/W.
errors.paper: There are s child calls, each on a stream of volume V/W; s/W is the normalized ratio after dividing by V.

errors.says: The network turns C^{tensor D} into s_c calls on D/m axes.
errors.paper: The network acts on a group of e=mf axes with s_c children on e/m axes; D is first reduced by q_0 row chunks and split into base-m pieces.

errors.says: Each edge difference is a product of two-point kernels aI+bX_v, and telescoping gives C^{tensor m} on every role.
errors.paper: Each factor is aI+bX_v or its inverse, one per orthonormal residual basis vector; C^{tensor m} holds only after source and sink diagonal corrections and undoing the signed exchange.

errors.says: For coprime s<t, A and B_0 are contractions computable in O(tp^{3/2+delta}alpha).
errors.paper: It requires theta=t/s-1>p/alpha^4 and other bounds; only approximations with error below p^2 are computed in that time.

errors.says: Applies H_0 to the same bit position in d address chunks.
errors.paper: The layer acts on D<=d chunks.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route: toolkit, finite network, chunk interchange, simultaneous layer, retained-order convolution, resampling with retained permutations, the algorithm and the cost table, ending at O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}). It thins out at the source of the saving. S1.3.3 asserts s<Wm with no label budget Wm-2N+2L or L<N/2, and tau=1-2^{-50} is never derived, so the strict inequality that drives both recurrences is taken on trust. The layer recurrence (S3.3) and the error chain (S6.6) are also only asserted.

steps.note: S1.3.1 has triples of a ground set, the exchange (X,Y)->(-Y,X) and restored scratch wires. It never fixes h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3 or m=h^3, so the dimension m in s<Wm is unanchored.
S1.3.2 states that a common invertible frame per gate commutes with pointwise linear gates, giving D_out S D_in^{-1} with edge cost D_vD_u^{-1}.

S1.3.3 names nested nondegenerate subspaces of an m-dimensional space (and quotes 'comparable labels'). The ambient F^{tensor 3} and the key fact that only central wires from time 3 to 4 decrease, each losing h, are missing.
S1.3.3 juxtaposes subspace labels with edge-difference ranks, but never gives rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U or the N rank-one source exceptions.
No step gives sum|Delta dim|=Wm-2N+2L, L=Ich or s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
The conclusion s<Wm is stated repeatedly, but L/N=100/539 or 101/539 and the deficit N-2L>0 that produces it are absent.
S1.3.4 states that the rational matrices have endpoint difference I_m, so every role undergoes H<-H+D, in its role as the bit interface.
S2.1 and S2.2 give E_1 Pi E_2 and exactly a interchanges plus O(V), and S2.3 does each edge by smaller interchanges with ratio s/W, so a node makes s calls.

S2.3 has the correct recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) on volume V/W and O(Ve^tau) from s/W<m^tau. The exponent tau=1-2^{-50} and its derivation from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20 are absent, so conservatively this counts as mentioned.

central.summary: P06 reconstructs the frame principle (C2), the endpoint shear identity (C7) and the recursion by rank-counted interchanges (C8), and has the right recurrence shape. The middle of the chain is missing: the label construction with its single decreasing edge type (C3), rank equals dimension change (C4), the budget Wm-2N+2L (C5) and L/N<1/2 (C6). As a result s<Wm is asserted rather than explained, and the explicit tau is never obtained.
